item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find strong 2024 evidence that AMLO created a new, credible civilian oversight regime for the military or intelligence services. I also did not find reliable evidence that complaint systems were meaningfully upgraded to force independent investigation of protected actors; the record is mostly formal mechanisms plus persistent failure.","evidence":[{"title":"Mecanismos para presentar quejas y denuncias","publisher":"Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno","date":"2018-10-04","url":"https://www.gob.mx/buengobierno/documentos/mecanismos-para-presentar-quejas-y-denuncias","summary":"The federal government maintained a formal channel for complaints and denunciations against federal public servants, with internal control handling and follow-up. This shows a complaint-handling system existed, though it is generic rather than abuse-specific.","question_ids":["3B.4"]},{"title":"Del procedimiento ante la Comisión Nacional de los Derechos Humanos","publisher":"Orden Jurídico Nacional","date":"1994","url":"https://www.ordenjuridico.gob.mx/Documentos/Federal/html/wo15531.html","summary":"The CNDH framework allows any person, including relatives or NGOs, to file complaints about human-rights violations and bars executive instructions to the commission. That is formal civilian oversight architecture, but the source is legal structure rather than proof of effective 2024 enforcement.","question_ids":["3B.4"]},{"title":"Que es la Visitaduría General","publisher":"Fiscalía General de la República","date":"2016","url":"https://www.gob.mx/fgr/acciones-y-programas/que-es-la-visitaduria-general","summary":"The FGR’s Visitaduría/complaint system accepts grievances against federal prosecutors and can receive and track denunciations. This is a real oversight and complaint mechanism, but it mainly shows availability, not independence or results in high-level abuse cases.","question_ids":["3B.4"]},{"title":"Presidente AMLO entregará informe a madres y padres Ayotzinapa con anexos que sustentan cada respuesta","publisher":"Secretaría de Gobernación","date":"2024-07-03","url":"https://www.gob.mx/segob/prensa/presidente-amlo-entregara-informe-a-madres-y-padres-ayotzinapa-con-anexos-que-sustentan-cada-respuesta-370094","summary":"The government said it had searched 251 sites and handled 141 cases in the Ayotzinapa process, presenting an updated report to families. This is evidence of continued case handling and some investigative activity, but not proof of independent accountability for protected actors.","question_ids":["3B.4","2B.9"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Mexico","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico","summary":"HRW says civilian killings by the army are rarely independently investigated, military obstruction impeded Ayotzinapa and Cold War abuse inquiries, and intelligence services withheld documents. This is strong evidence against effective civilian oversight and independent investigation.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"World Report 2025: Mexico","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2025","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/mexico","summary":"HRW says soldiers were implicated in torture, arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, and enforced disappearances, with limited civilian oversight; it also says the 2024 constitutional changes expanded military power and permitted indefinite domestic deployment. That is strong evidence the accountability architecture remained weak or worsened.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.2","3B.1"]},{"title":"Mexico: Flawed Inquiry on Soldiers’ Alleged Killing of Child","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-08-28","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/28/mexico-flawed-inquiry-on-soldiers-alleged-killing-of-child","summary":"HRW says the Attorney General’s Office failed to properly investigate a 2022 killing allegedly involving soldiers, ignored inconsistencies, and missed basic corroboration steps. This is direct evidence of deficient independent investigation of military abuse.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Informe Mundial 2024: México","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/es/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico","summary":"The report says torture is common, arbitrary detention remains widespread, and Army/Navy detentions are still not always recorded in the national registry. That points to weak due process and poor tracking of abuse by security forces.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Mexico: Killings of journalists under state protection show urgent need to strengthen federal mechanism","publisher":"Amnesty International / CPJ","date":"2024-03-06","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/mexico-killings-journalists-strengthen-federal-mechanism/","summary":"Amnesty says journalists enrolled in the federal protection mechanism were still being killed, showing the protection system was not functioning as an effective accountability or prevention mechanism.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.3"]},{"title":"Mexico","publisher":"ONU-DH / UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention","date":"2024-09-17","url":"https://hchr.org.mx/relatorias_grupos/visita-a-mexico-informe-del-grupo-de-trabajo-sobre-la-detencion-arbitraria/","summary":"The UN Working Group said arbitrary detention remained widespread and linked to ill-treatment, torture, disappearances, and arbitrary executions, while military and navy detentions were not always entered in the registry. That is direct negative evidence on due process and oversight.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]}]}
